### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.cursorword

### Question

Hello,

I’ve been using mini.cursorword for several months and have been very happy with the default behavior, particularly the automatic highlighting of the word under the cursor.

Recently, I experimented with customizing the highlight group. Instead of the default underline style, I changed it to use a background block-style highlight (which I believe is also a fairly common preference).

```lua
    vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, "MiniCursorword", { link = "Visual" })
    vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, "MiniCursorwordCurrent", { link = "MiniCursorword" })
```

However, after making this change, I noticed some unexpected behavior when performing search and replace operations using `:%s//`. The highlight from mini.cursorword remains active and appears to visually clash with Vim’s default search highlight groups during the substitution process.

I’m wondering whether this interaction is expected by design, or if there is a recommended way to avoid this kind of highlight conflict when customizing the highlight style.

As a workaround, I temporarily disable mini.cursorword in command-line mode:

```lua
    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("CmdlineEnter", {
      desc = "Disable mini.cursorword in command mode",
      callback = function()
        vim.b.minicursorword_disable = true
      end,
    })

    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("CmdlineLeave", {
      desc = "Re-enable mini.cursorword after command mode",
      callback = function()
        vim.b.minicursorword_disable = false
      end,
    })
```

This resolves the visual conflict for me, but I’m not sure if this is the intended approach.

Thank you for the work on the plugin btw, it’s been a great addition to my setup.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for kind words!

> However, after making this change, I noticed some unexpected behavior when performing search and replace operations using `:%s//`. The highlight from mini.cursorword remains active and appears to visually clash with Vim’s default search highlight groups during the substitution process.
> 
> I’m wondering whether this interaction is expected by design, or if there is a recommended way to avoid this kind of highlight conflict when customizing the highlight style.

I can reproduce. This is not the result of customizing highlight groups, by the way, as the same behavior is seen with default underline groups.

No, it is not explicitly intended, but I have a feeling that this will be impossible to adjust on the 'mini.cursorword' side. The module already tries to be respectful of not being on top of other important highlighting, like when searching with `/`. It is done by explicitly setting very small match priority for both [current](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/4e61631464a12138bc0c82ea216b1d0d3cc2b315/lua/mini/cursorword.lua#L241) and [other](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/4e61631464a12138bc0c82ea216b1d0d3cc2b315/lua/mini/cursorword.lua#L253) matches.

It seems that `:%s/` doesn't quite respect this priority and/or has a priority even lower than `-1`. My guess is that this is an issue in Vim (not even Neovim), but it needs extra confirmation.

reply_data.body:
I tried reproducing this using pure `matchadd()` with a negative priority in both Vim and Neovim (without `mini.cursorword`).

In Neovim, `/` search highlighting respects the match priority and overrides it as expected, but the `:%s` preview highlighting does not seem to do so.

In Vim, the behavior is different again — `/` search does not override the `matchadd()` highlight in the same way.

So this appears to be editor-level behavior rather than something specific to `mini.cursorword`.

Thanks again for the explanation.. i’ll stick with the command-line mode workaround on my end.

> In Neovim, `/` search highlighting respects the match priority and overrides it as expected, but the `:%s` preview highlighting does not seem to do so.

I *think* it is not an expected behavior and better reported to 'neovim/neovim' as an issue. My expectation would be that both 'hlsearch' and 'incsearch' have the same behavior when interacting with `matchadd` highlighting.

But yeah, I don't think there is anything to be done on 'mini.cursorword' side.
